notes.title: Community Update #13: Working the Workbench and Release Update
notes.content:
Hi Fellow Racketeers,

This time around we'll look at how the work on the workbench is progress (nice stuff Darren) and an updat on release timing.

Working the Workbench

Darren's been doing lots of things, but he's finally got his head out of the lighting game and into going over and putting together Jimmy's Workbench. As a reminder, this is where Jimmy cleans up goods before moving them on to limit his 'Heat' level and hopefully avoid the worst of nosey cops.

Jimmy can upgrade the bench with a range of items that ensure he can improve his ability to reduce the heat of an item. Some upgrades only work on certain item categories (you just can't use the soldering iron on a jacket), whilst some are more universal.

Below is the latest render of the workbench.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679598/06fe9e2b8306c0d4da4a4ccf6c17d05265b2c3f4.png

Release Timing

I'd like to say we are steaming towards a Q3 release, but I just can't lie to you. With our little part time dev team, real life has just gotten in the way and we have also needed more time on some of the game elements we're working on. Whilst it's all in the name of ensuring you get a polished product, it does mean we need to let it cook as long as it takes.

To that end I hope to give an updated release timeframe in the coming month or so.

Next Community Updates

For next time we'll have a little look at some of the upgrades for the workbench and what each of them do!

Keep hustlin',

Anthony

notes.title: Fence Community Update #10
notes.content:
Post Easter Work

Hello Fellow Racketeers!

This week, we'll check back in with Darren who's been working on getting Jimmy's streeet in the Bronx looking just right. 

Day and Night

Part of keeping the Bronx real is having a true day/night cycle for Jimmy to navigate. Day and night lighting aren't only about asthetics, but also determine who is about/available to trade with and influences police presence. Importantly, the night lighting scheme is about conveying that maybe the streets aren't the safest after dark....

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679598/5be062984e78af8daabc611f0ee8014cc45f2b93.jpg
One of the unique aspects of New York's streetscape is the many a differing Bodegas. Lots of research revealed there are so many types in different styles, but what Darren has developed looks both authentic and fitting for Jimmy's neighbourhood.

Similarly, the exterior of Shifty Adam's Bar needed to be a welcoming oasis in the night time, but still looking appropriate for the area. We think it looks just right!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679598/dbc11137913c0d7198081f8b1af917a9ef98378d.jpg
Next time, we might look at more of our NPCs who you'll run into or maybe some of the collections of 'hot items' Jimmy can try and collect for profit and put in his scrapbook.

Keep hustlin'

- Anthony (Lead Designer)

notes.title: Fence Community Update #9
notes.content:
Happy Easter!

Happy Easter Fellow Racketeers!

This week, I thought I'd introduce you to Cesar - our suave Latino on the street.

Cesar

Cesar (or sometimes spelt Caesar) was a pretty common name within the New York Latino community in the 1980's and 1990's. Elena has lovingly created our own 'Cesar' in the game to be the typical (over-)confident, charming and well dressed (well he thinks so!) street Latino in The Bronx. Cesar isn't a gangster or hood, but is morally flexible enough to pick up anything left lying around to sell to Jimmy for a few bucks.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679598/dd993528ddfe5af09b76ce31a3008a2efa289acc.png
Like all of the characters that Jimmy can buy from or sell to, you'll have to work out what you can get a bit cheaper from Caesar (he probably doesn't want much to do with drugs or guns!) and what he'll want top dollar for.

Next time, we'll catch back up with where Darren has gotten to with lighting the streets!

Keep hustlin'

- Anthony (Lead Designer)

notes.title: Fence Community Update #8
notes.content:
April 2025 - We keep going

Hi Fellow Racketeers!

In this second week of April the team has continued on with programming the mission systems, lighting and character art. This week I'm going to focus on Darren's lighting work in and around Shifty's.

Lighting for Effect - Shifty Adam's Bar

At first glance lighting can seem like, 'just put in a sun and some lights where they should be indoors and it should look fine?'. Of course you could do this, but we've tried to make each location's lighting convey the right mood, highlight interactables, as well as bring out the 'character' of the environment.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679598/00688749a92a1ce89826e838b4a4a149b66068f4.jpg
In Shifty Adam's, where Jimmy is trying to 'hock' stolen wares, we wanted a dingy bar with the sort of clientele that wouldn't mind a 'cheap' TV. Plenty of 'research' went into what a 'dingy bar' is like!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679598/fd462363d64231167b689a7c936b40e6c2c672b5.jpg
Next time, we'll have a look at what our Lead Charcter Artist, Elena has created with our Hispanic wannabe mucho 'Ceasar'.

Keep hustlin'

- Anthony (Lead Designer)

notes.title: Fence Community Update #7
notes.content:
Into April 2025

Hi fellow Shifters of 'Five Finger Discounted' Goods!

This week the team has continued to work on a range of items. I thought it might be interesting to focus this update on one of our NPC Characters, Sarah: the preppy 'Kelpto'.

Sarah: The Preppy Klepto

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679598/b4c7c84764e2f0fce8d17700fa777cd03aaf74dc.jpg
Sarah is one of the NPC's you can buy hot goods from. As a bored preppy school girl from a 'good family' she spices up the monotony of trying to be the perfect Preppy Girl by seeing what an how much she can 'lift' from various stores, school bags and lockers without being caught.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679598/35c837bc9731e600545ddabbcf1becb0bab8fe9c.jpg
Jimmy can bargain with Sarah to help her turn her Kelpto hobby into cash....of course, Sarah doesn't seem to deal in guns or drugs.

Timing Is Everything

Part of making Jimmy's world 'real' is the realistic and meaningful timing of our NPCs locations and availabiliy. For example, Sarah is not available to trade with during school hours as she is (of course) at school. Part of the game is considering 'when' certain types of characters are available to optimise trading outcomes and likelihood of getting certain items.

Next time, we might dip into an update on where Darren is up to with lighting.

Keep hustlin'

- Anthony (Lead Designer)

notes.title: Fence Community Update #6
notes.content:
Hitting the Ground Running in 2026

Hi fellow Racketeers!

We've been steadily progressing along since the start of the year despite some disruption due to Cyclone Alfred. We thought a short update was in order!

Lighting for The Bronx

To kick off 2026, Darren has been learning, experimenting and optimising the game's lighting design. A critical part of the lighting design is ensuring we create the ideal visual ambience to help convey Jimmy story and help our players identify the things thay can do next.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679598/a887c8eff1676361f029c7732359c8622fb8389c.jpg

Well behaved NPCs 

Dan has finished programming our improved NPC behaviour system. After some population of the extensive behaviour data tables, what we hopefully have is a world that looks 'lived in' and where our NPCs do more than just interact with the main character (Jimmy).

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679598/775e154f32c694de2b8c164942ce7983e9c4d484.jpg

Mission System Development

Also keeping Dan Busy is further refining the mission system with the addition of time based limits relevant to some of the mission sets we have.

How far along are we?

Great question! We have completed most of the planned systems (80%), environmental art and character art, with the main jobs left to do being the mission system, ledger (yes, there is a ledger!) and some upgrading capability. In fact, if you you just want to 'sandbox' play, that is all pretty much in place now!

We are keen to release the game in Q3 2025 (this year), but also want to ensure that Jimmy and his world are a (relatively) bug free, high quality experience. To that end we will keep you informed as to our progress.

Our next update wont be too far away and I'm hoping we can show off a few of the wonderful NPCs that Elena has been working on.

Keep hustlin'

- Anthony (Lead Designer)

notes.title: Fence Community Update #4
notes.content:
Hi There!

Dan here, Its been a little while! Sorry for the delayed update - We have been incredibly busy this month! 

Lets jump right in!

Bodega Business

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679598/20e5be1b484b83eec27afe89ebce09a083816722.png

Darren has been hard at work on the Bodega the past week or so. It's all in engine now with some gorgeous materials. A big part of the building assets in Fence is to bind the player to the 90's Bronx setting, so this is a big step in that direction!

Missions

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679598/828970a9d38514891271fb5cce9c8322f6ab46e0.png

I've completed the fundamental mechanics of our missions/quest system. We took a bit more time with this one as we need it to be pretty extendible, and dynamically affect the world as the player progresses (Item Prices, NPC Schedules, Buildings etc).

It's currently set up with a Work in progress UI, and will be filling it out with content over the next month or so.


Inventory Improvements

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679598/c03d095a58256f3fa6eea895169f6c24b941d797.png

We've done some work on our player and world inventory system and UI - Adding a tooltip so the player can get a bit more item information. At the moments it's just displaying name & item condition, but in future it will display a bit more information about Sale price, profit, and other details, potentially based off Jimmy's skill levels.

Dev Stream & Socials

Anthony has thrown around the idea of doing a fortnightly dev stream! We are currently planning out what we'd like to show off for it, and what platforms it will be on, so stay tuned for that.

We've also set up a bunch of socials that we will be pretty active on for exclusive content, you should be able to find those on our Steam page!

As always, if you haven't already, definitely go ahead and wishlist and follow the game, as we have much more update content planned for Fence towards release!

Cheers!

notes.title: Fence Community Update #3
notes.content:
Hello Again!

It’s been a productive week at On The Level this week. We have been wrapping up a few systems and key art assets, as well as added a significant amount of dialogue content to the game.

Release Plans

We’ve been looking at our release and publishing schedules quite a lot the past few weeks. We don’t have a definitive date for release yet, however we are looking around Q2-3 2025, Much of our release timing at the moment is based around the steam summer sale. Launching before it provides some opportunities to get the game to you guys with a discount from go, as well as a nice discount in the summer sale, as we want to give you guys the best bang for buck we can on release.

It also proves some challenges around visibility and eligibility (Particularly for our Next Fest timing), but these are challenges that we are fleshing out and making decisions on at the movement. We'll be sure to update you all on this date as soon as we have a final date come in!

Dialogue

Anthony has got a lot of the key dialogue systems and content in and running. At this stage we have around 8 NPC’s with pretty fleshed out dialogues to them. Each NPC has around 15 of their own unique dialogue trees to draw from, some of which have 2-3 random variations to the dialogue - this means each NPC has around 50-80 unique dialogues!

This has proven to be a lot of work - especially when you pair it with Unreal Engines horrendous editor for data tables. We originally considered developing a solution early on to kind of ‘wizardize’ it and create a tool for baking dialogues into a data table through a step-by-step wizard like dialogue builder, but we figured that we didn’t have that many NPC’s in total, and we also wanted very fleshed out quality dialogue, so the rate at which we were finalising them wasn’t as important to our ability to easily re-iterate on them and test/view them in game. 


The World

A fair bit of work has gone into the world of Fence over the past couple of months, our level design has been pretty well done for some time, but it still is receiving new assets and features. One upcoming highlight is the Bodega. Darren has been hard at work with the initial art and material design for it, and it will hit the streetscape soon.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679598/61fa47899a35a6190a8e40fd7af39eb22115ab44.png

I thought I’d also shoot into one of our earlier builds and grab some screenshots to do a comparison on how Darren has evolved our level design from the initial design blockout

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679598/8330e6b29560e967f6df095a36630db16e440c48.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679598/f855eb231ded432d9adb217cf2e87276e3f58286.png

That is it for today! Be sure to drop a follow and a wishlist if you are keen on getting to know more about the game!

If you have any questions or would like to join the Fence community, come visit us on Discord and say hello!

- Dan

notes.title: Fence Community Update #2
notes.content:
Hi There!

The team has been hard at work this past week, bringing a few key systems and art assets to life in Fence. Darren and Elena have been creating some environmental and character assets, while Dan and Anthony have been focused on developing the NPC dialogue systems that will bring more depth and personality to the game.

Extra! Extra!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679598/e801e5d953a15af577659f843a39c63e87f894a9.jpg

Here’s a sneak peek at one of the environmental art pieces Darren has been working on: the Newspaper vending machine. This isn’t just for show—this mechanic will let Jimmy grab a fresh newspaper each week, providing a detailed list of events affecting gameplay. The stories on these pages, found in the Newspaper Events, offer valuable clues on global modifiers, setting details, and deeper game lore set in 1990s New York. Keep an eye on these papers to get a leg up in the game!

Hey Jimmy, That You?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679598/de743dd872ec7c1b9aadc0222cd835da7673f9d0.gif

Our NPC dialogue system is coming together nicely! We’re working on giving each NPC their own unique voice and personality. This week, we’ve been focusing on the dialogue for NPCs who buy and sell items. Each of these characters will have distinct dialogue reflecting the kinds of goods they prefer, whether it’s luxury items, street essentials, or something more unique. This will not only add to the immersion but also help you strategize about who to approach with specific items in your inventory.


If you haven’t already, join our community on Discord to share your ideas and stay updated with exclusive content. Don’t forget to wishlist Fence on Steam to be the first to know when we go live.

Until next time.

The On The Level Team.

notes.title: Fence Community Update #1
notes.content:
What’s up, Scroungers!

We’re excited to kick off a new weekly update series to keep you all in the loop about the progress we're making on Fence. Each week, we’ll be diving into the milestones we’ve hit, sharing key decisions the team has made, and giving you a sneak peek at the cool things we’ve been working on.

As for what to call these updates, we’ve been tossing around names like "Scroungers Wrap-Up" or "The Fence Weekly Ledger"—but we want to hear from you! If you have any creative ideas that match the game’s gritty, underground vibe, drop them in the comments. We’d love to see what you come up with!

Progress

This week, we’re highlighting the fantastic work from our art team, particularly our Character Artist, Elena. She’s been hard at work designing two key characters for the story: Lloyd and Tyler.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44679598/ec8a29262850635a88c7b0ab57ea962c997c06f5.png

Here’s a sneak peek at Lloyd (left) and Tyler (right), both members of the Bloods gang. You’ll be running into them throughout the game. Tyler is a young, edgy, wannabe tough guy who’s trying hard to prove himself, while Lloyd, an already established Blood member, is rational, and knows that success lies in having the right goods, and getting your hands on cheap produce to move on the street.

Keeping a good rep with both Lloyd and Tyler is paramount to establishing yourself as a successful fence in the Bronx. If you can prove yourself capable of handling the tasks they put forward, you’ll unlock new opportunities and build trust, which is essential for climbing the ranks in the unforgiving world that is Fence.

Status of Development

Work within the other teams is chugging away at a good pace. We are at a pretty decent spot right now in terms of gameplay, with many fundamental features and aspects of the game coming together. Make sure you wishlist, and join our Discord community for more updates to come.

Until next time!

The On The Level Team

What's Next?

Keep Hustling,

The On The Level Team.
